traditional.pt: Zacarias, filho de Berequias e neto de Ido (1:1), profeta do retorno do exílio. Ed 5:1 e 6:14 o ligam a Ageu.
traditional.en: Zechariah, son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo (1:1), a prophet of the return from exile. Ezra 5:1 and 6:14 link him with Haggai.

scholarly.pt: Os caps. 1–8 são atribuídos ao profeta, e os caps. 9–14 costumam ser vistos como obra posterior, de outra mão ou escola, com datas debatidas. Não há consenso sobre a unidade do livro.
scholarly.en: Chapters 1–8 are attributed to the prophet, and chs. 9–14 are usually seen as a later work, from another hand or school, with debated dates. There is no consensus on the unity of the book.

traditional.pt: Os caps. 1–8 são datados nos anos 520–518 a.C. (1:1; 1:7; 7:1), no reinado de Dario.
traditional.en: Chapters 1–8 are dated to 520–518 BC (1:1; 1:7; 7:1), in the reign of Darius.

scholarly.pt: Caps. 1–8: c. 520–518 a.C.; caps. 9–14: período persa tardio ou helenístico, em propostas variadas.
scholarly.en: Chs. 1–8: c. 520–518 BC; chs. 9–14: late Persian or Hellenistic period, in various proposals.

recipients.pt: A comunidade que voltou do exílio, em especial Zorobabel e o sumo sacerdote Josué.
recipients.en: The community that returned from exile, especially Zerubbabel and the high priest Joshua.

theme.pt: A restauração de Jerusalém e do templo pelo Espírito de Deus, com visões noturnas, o futuro rei humilde e o pastor ferido.
theme.en: The restoration of Jerusalem and the temple by God's Spirit, with night visions, the humble future king and the struck shepherd.

historicalContext.pt: O livro mistura visões simbólicas (1:7–6:8) com oráculos de esperança. Os caps. 9–14 trazem imagens, como o rei humilde (9:9), o pastor ferido (13:7) e aquele a quem traspassaram (12:10), que o Novo Testamento relê. A interpretação dessas passagens é muito discutida.
historicalContext.en: The book mixes symbolic visions (1:7–6:8) with oracles of hope. Chapters 9–14 bring images such as the humble king (9:9), the struck shepherd (13:7) and the one they pierced (12:10), which the New Testament rereads. The interpretation of these passages is much discussed.

title.pt: A questão do jejum e promessas
title.en: The question of fasting and promises

title.pt: Primeiro oráculo: o rei e o pastor
title.en: First oracle: the king and the shepherd

title.pt: Segundo oráculo: Jerusalém e o dia do Senhor
title.en: Second oracle: Jerusalem and the day of the Lord

connections.pt: Mt 21:5 e Jo 12:15 citam Zc 9:9. Mt 26:31 cita Zc 13:7. Jo 19:37 cita Zc 12:10. Mt 27:9–10 relaciona Zc 11:12–13 a Jeremias. Ap usa imagens de Zacarias, como os cavalos e as lâmpadas.
connections.en: Matt 21:5 and John 12:15 quote Zech 9:9. Matt 26:31 quotes Zech 13:7. John 19:37 quotes Zech 12:10. Matt 27:9–10 relates Zech 11:12–13 to Jeremiah. Revelation uses images from Zechariah, such as the horses and the lampstands.
